title: Stand an electric toothbrush on its charger: the handle's hollow base lowered straight over the hidden charging post
instruction: Stand the electric toothbrush on its charger: pick up the handle, lower its base straight down over the charger's post, and let go so it stands on the charger by itself.
context: Most UK adults brush with an electric toothbrush: 59% in the Office for Health Improvement and Disparities survey, two in three in the 2020 Oral Health Foundation and Oral-B study (US: 23%, YouGov). After brushing it goes back on its charger; Braun's manual says only: place the toothbrush handle on the charging unit. A short post on the charger fits a hollow in the handle's base. No walls guide it: the hand must hold the tall, light handle upright, centre its base over a post 10 mm across that the base itself hides once close, lower it straight, and let go so it stands on its own. Let go tilted, it rests on the post's tip and topples; pushed off-centre, the light charger slides across the counter.
setup: Metres; x forward, y to the robot's left, z up; origin midway between the arm bases (0, +/-0.305); the counter is the bench top (z = 0.7475). (1) Braun Oral-B Type 3757 charger, free: a white rounded block 65 x 55 x 33 mm (reseller listing), 0.10 kg, friction 0.6 static, 0.5 dynamic (rubber feet; estimates), centred at (0.40, -0.02), its 65 mm along x; a post 10 mm across and 13 mm tall, its top 3 mm tapered to 6 mm across, at the middle of its top (estimate). (2) Oral-B Pro-series handle with its brush head fitted, free, one rigid body: body 27 mm across and 170 mm long, neck and head to 232 mm, 0.13 kg, friction 0.6 static, 0.5 dynamic; in its base a recess 11 mm across (16-sided, 0.5 mm clearance a side round the post) and 14 mm deep (all estimates). It lies on its side along y, its base's centre at (0.40, -0.32), head toward the charger (+y), its body's middle about 21 cm right of the charger. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. The README lists every collider. Real trial: the same handle and charger, plugged in, with tape round the charger's feet and a phone filming the side beside a millimetre scale.
scoring: Read from the state at the end of the run; only the failures latch, so a step undone loses its credit. 0.33: the handle lifted (base over 10 mm above the counter) with its axis within 15 degrees of vertical, base down. 0.67: upright, its base's centre within 3 mm of the post's axis and at most 12 mm above the charger's top, so the post is inside the recess (real trial: a side photo against a millimetre scale). 1.0: on the post with the base within 2 mm of the charger's top, tilt under 5 degrees, still, and every part of both grippers 20 mm or more from the handle, for 2 s running (real trial: it stands by itself, a phone level reads under 5 degrees, the charge light flashes). Void (0): the charger pushed over 20 mm off its mark or tipped over 20 degrees, or the handle dropped after it is lifted (its base falling faster than 0.3 m/s and 0.15 m/s faster than both hands move down: a release, about 5 mm of free fall). Real trial: in the side video, the frame where the fingers open shows the base no more than 5 mm above the charger's top on the mm scale. Possible scores: 0, 0.33, 0.67, 1.0.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo reaches 1.0 at step 404 (20.2 s).
reset_notes: Nothing is random. Lift the handle off the charger and lay it on its side at its tape mark, head toward the charger; put the charger back in its tape marks; both arms at their ready pose. About 1 minute.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at the sizes in setup; unpublished sizes (the post, the recess, the handle) are estimates. The handle with its head is one body of uniform density, so its centre of mass may sit higher than a real one's. Charging is not modelled: a seated handle is read from the geometry. A drop is read from the base's falling speed against the hands' downward speed after every physics step. The hands-clear test reads a point lattice over each whole gripper against the handle's exact envelope.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (valid, one session, 1,200 steps). Demo: 1.0 (one hand, 404 steps, 20.2 s, GPU). Kept hold on the post 0.67; set on the charger beside the post 0.33; stood on the counter 0; let go tilted on the post's tip 0 (topples); let go 20 mm above the post 0 (drop); nothing 0.
